elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: New §5.5: "The Company owns all deliverables and work product created for the Company under this Agreement, including the Site (the 'Deliverables')".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: §5.5: "HDI hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in the Deliverables and such work product" — present-tense assignment, correct party direction (Vendor to Customer).

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: §5.5: "grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use any HDI intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: §5.5 grants an "irrevocable" licence to embedded HDI IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: §5.5 grants a "royalty-free" licence to embedded HDI IP.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: §5.5: "The Company retains all right, title and interest in all Content and all customer, user and transaction data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company in connection with the Site ('Company Data')" — the belonging-to/supplied-by/processed-for formulation captures every category, not selected data types.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: §5.5: "any license of HDI in Company Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the services under this Agreement". The only exception is "except as the Company approves under Section 7.1" — an affirmative, Customer-controlled consent gate, not a standing Vendor right to distribute, resell or independently exploit Company Data, so the limitation holds absent our approval.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: §5.5 closing sentence: "No intellectual property is owned jointly by the Parties."

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: §5.5 expressly preserves HDI's pre-existing intellectual property, which encompasses its generic tools and know-how existing before the engagement; nothing in the insert strips HDI of them.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Exceeded rather than granted: the Company takes outright ownership by assignment of "all right, title and interest in the Deliverables", which is inherently perpetual; no separate licence term is needed.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Assignment of all right, title and interest is not revocable; ownership subsumes an irrevocable licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Unqualified assignment of "all right, title and interest" carries no territorial limit.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No royalty, fee or ongoing consideration is attached to the assignment or to the embedded-IP licence (expressly "royalty-free").

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: As owner of the Deliverables with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded HDI IP, the Company may use and modify them without restriction; §5.2's exclusive artistic and editorial control is retained and consistent.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Ownership of all right, title and interest carries the right to sublicense; no field-of-use or exclusivity restriction in favour of HDI survives the insert.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Same operative sentence in §5.5 limiting HDI's licence in Company Data to processing solely to provide the services, subject only to a Company-approval carve-out under §7.1.

elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Duplicate listing of the first preferred element; satisfied by the same §5.5 ownership sentence.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single inserted §5.5 delivers all nine preferred elements in operative language (Company ownership, HDI assignment, HDI pre-existing IP retained, perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence back, Company Data retention, HDI data licence limited to service provision, no joint ownership). Nothing is left to the margin comment.

The clause was genuinely missing — §§1.1, 2.1, 5.2 and the General Manager paragraph allocate work, content delivery and editorial control but no ownership — so a concise insertion is the minimal remedy even though all its words are new. No existing sentence is deleted or paraphrased, no survival tail, expense allocation, indemnity, damages category or procedural boilerplate is added, and the Company-favourable §5.2 editorial-control and approval language is retained intact.

Customer Data scope is correctly universal: "all Content and all customer, user and transaction data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company", rather than a list of selected data types, and no Vendor right to distribute, resell or independently exploit that data is created.

The §7.1 carve-out is Customer-consent-gated and preserves the reciprocal cross-promotion e-mail mechanic rather than contradicting it, so intent survives. Two mechanical checks the drafter should confirm before sending, neither of which changes the outcome here: (i) that Section 7.1 exists and in fact contains the Company-approval e-mail-list mechanic, so the cross-reference is not dangling; and (ii) that no Section 5.5 already exists in Article 5, so the numbering does not collide.

Optional tightening (rationale-level only, not a deviation): the embedded-IP licence back could add "worldwide" and an express sublicensing right for group companies and successors; as drafted the Company's outright ownership of the Deliverables already supplies unrestricted territorial and sublicensing scope, so this is not required for completeness.
